Xanthenone- 4-acetic acid mono- methyl analogues with substitutions in the seventh and eighth position of the molecule were the most active for cytokine induction and endothelial tube formation inhibition in human systems.

(i) XAA analogues are species-selective; (ii) the 5- and/or 6-substituents on the xanthenone backbone were the key structural features that conferred murine-selectivity; (iii) analogues with 7- or 8-methyl substitutions were the most active at stimulating human cytokine production and at inhibiting human endothelial tube formation; (iv) 5- or 6-methyl substitutions were inactive in human systems,

the 5,6- and 7-substituted XAA analogues were most effective at inducing murine cytokine production, whereas the 7- and 8-substituted analogs were most effective at stimulating human cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 7-methyl analogue of XAA, DMXAA, was the most active compound in murine cell and animal models and is now in clinical trials.

the 5- and the 6-substitution positions on the XAA backbone appear to be the most important for activity in murine models while the 7- and 8-substitution positions appear to be the main positions that confer human cell activity.
the 5- and/or 6-methyl substituted XAA analogues are likely to be the most promising for future clinical development.
